source.title: Transcoder-based Circuit Analysis for Interpretable Single-Cell Foundation Models
source.authors: Sosuke Hosokawa; Toshiharu Kawakami; S. Kodera; M. Ito; Norihiko Takeda

record.tranche_reason: Applies transcoder-based feature extraction and circuit tracing in a single-cell foundation model, a new model setting, and reports feature interpretability results relevant to dictionary-recovered features.
record.gate_note: The study reports feature-interpretation and circuit-tracing outcomes relevant to V4. The transcoder replacement validation loss and KL comparisons assess functional approximation, not whether the claim's feature geometry or dictionary features hold, so they are not included as claim rows. The cited results from prior work are not treated as findings of this study.
record.test_reason: The study uses transcoders as an interpretability tool on C2S-Pythia-410m and reports how well its own pipeline works: 7/20 features interpretable and one illustrative circuit. Polysemanticity and superposition appear only as cited motivation. There is no neuron baseline, no random or untrained-transcoder control, and no measure of features being spread across neurons. Its results therefore do not bear on whether V4 holds; they show only that the tool gave some interpretable output in this setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that transcoders extract biologically interpretable features and decision circuits from C2S. They note two limits: interpretation was manual and subjective, and the choice of training dataset strongly affects the learned features. They also say the circuit remains large and complex.
record.recipe_differences: Uses trained transcoders and circuit attribution on a single-cell foundation model; it does not reproduce the toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that the training dataset can significantly affect learned features and circuits; only Heart Cell Atlas v2 was used.

fits_no_version.finding: In a layer-12 transcoder (8192 latents) on C2S-Pythia-410m, 7 of 20 randomly sampled live features consistently fired on tokens of specific genes or gene families. Many of these are sub-word token features. No neuron baseline is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transcoder features in single-cell foundation models are partly interpretable at the gene level (method-performance claim, not superposition).

fits_no_version.finding: A traced circuit for endothelial classification includes features on the endothelial marker genes VWF, PTPRB and SPARCL1, but is large and mostly hard to interpret.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transcoder circuit tracing recovers biologically plausible components in scFMs.

record.problems: The feature-interpretation result is based on a random sample of 20 layer-12 features and manual interpretation. The circuit analysis is illustrated with a single cell-type classification case; the authors describe the circuit as large and complex. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions.
No test of polysemanticity arising from other causes.
Does not measure whether features are distributed across neurons. Does not compare dictionary features with neurons, so dictionary recovery of sparse features is not tested.
Input-invariance of transcoder features is asserted from prior work, not tested. Completeness, stability and canonicality are not evaluated.
No comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' and its V4 labels are overturned. This is an application paper that relies on SAE/transcoder methods without testing the superposition claim. The validation loss (2.48 original vs 4.63 transcoder vs 12.67 no-MLP) and KL 2.41 show substantial reconstruction loss, which is also relevant only to method quality.

versions.untested_parts: No tests of toy-network superposition, feature overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometric arrangements.
Polysemanticity and transcoder features are discussed, but the study does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
No test of whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
Tests transcoder feature recovery in one single-cell foundation model, not feature distribution across neurons or the generality of sparse feature recovery across LLMs and models.
Input-invariance is described, but completeness, stability, and canonical status of the recovered features are not evaluated.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: vandijklab/C2S-Pythia-410m-cell-type-prediction
rows.operation_detail: Human interpretation of randomly selected transcoder features
rows.measure: Number and proportion of sampled features classified as gene-level interpretable
rows.value: 7 out of 20 features (35%) were gene-level interpretable
rows.note: Features were judged by which tokens activated them; a feature counted as gene-level interpretable if it consistently activated on tokens for specific genes or gene families.
rows.check: Reports interpretability of the study's own transcoder features (7/20 gene-level interpretable) with no baseline. There is no comparison to MLP neurons or a control dictionary, so it cannot show sparse features beyond what neurons already give. Many 'interpretable' features are sub-word tokenizer pieces rather than gene concepts.

rows.subject: vandijklab/C2S-Pythia-410m-cell-type-prediction
rows.operation_detail: Traced a transcoder circuit for feature 3353 activated during endothelial-cell classification

conditions.value: 128-gene endothelial-cell prompt from Heart Cell Atlas v2
feature 3353 on the final token in the last layer

rows.measure: Biological interpretation of gene-token features in the extracted circuit
rows.value: The circuit showed strong contributions from features associated with VWF, PTPRB, and SPARCL1; the authors describe these as endothelial-related genes.
rows.note: The authors also report that the circuit contains many features, including many associated with prompt tokens, and remains large and complex.
rows.check: A single qualitative circuit case study of the authors' method, with no quantitative measure and no control. The authors note the circuit is large and complex, with many uninterpretable features. This is a method-demonstration result, not evidence on the claim.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
